description: Third-party advertisers can analyze browsing data to create detailed profiles of individual users based on their browsing patterns, interests, and behaviors. This enables linking of data across different contexts and services.
assumptions: Browsing data contains sufficient behavioral information for profiling

title: Quasi-identifier identification through browsing patterns
description: Browsing data contains combinations of attributes (pages visited, timing, sequence) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Browsing patterns are sufficiently unique to identify individuals

title: Dynamic set of third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers who may form a dynamic set of parties that changes frequently, increasing exposure risk beyond what users may expect.
assumptions: Advertiser relationships are not static and may change

title: Data propagation to external parties
description: Browsing data is propagated to third-party advertisers where it may be further processed, stored, or shared beyond the original purpose, creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: Advertisers may further process or share received data

title: User unawareness of browsing data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected by the AI recommendation engine and shared with third-party advertisers, especially if this is planned but not yet implemented with proper transparency.
assumptions: Users are not explicitly informed about this data flow

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or provide meaningful consent regarding how their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not be granular or user-friendly

title: Invalid consent for third-party data sharing
description: The sharing of browsing data with third-party advertisers may not rely on valid, informed consent, particularly if users are not clearly informed about the extent of data sharing or if consent is bundled with other terms.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet GDPR standards for third-party sharing

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may involve processing more personal data than is actually needed for the core functionality of the recommendation engine.
assumptions: Full browsing data may be shared when only aggregated or limited data would suffice

title: Linking through unique identifiers in transit
description: The data flow may contain unique identifiers (cookies, device IDs, user IDs) that can be used to link browsing data across different sessions and services during transmission.
assumptions: Browsing data includes persistent identifiers

title: Attributable browsing behavior evidence
description: Browsing data can be used to attribute specific browsing actions to individuals, preventing them from denying their online activities or interests.
assumptions: Browsing data can be reliably attributed to specific users

title: Processing of identified government ID data
description: Government ID images contain directly identified personal data (photo, name, ID number, date of birth, address) that is being stored in the file system. This constitutes processing of identified information.
assumptions: Government ID images contain standard identifying information

title: Unique identifier in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (ID numbers) that directly reference the identity of the data subject. Storage of these images preserves these identifiers.
assumptions: Government IDs contain unique identification numbers

title: Revealing attributes in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain multiple revealing attributes (photo, name, DOB, address, ID number) that support identification of the data subject. The combination of these attributes makes identification highly certain.
assumptions: Government ID images contain standard personal attributes

title: Linking through unique government ID identifier
description: The unique ID number in government ID images can be used to link this data with other data stores or systems that contain the same identifier, enabling cross-system data linkage.
assumptions: Government ID numbers are used as identifiers across multiple systems

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data containing biometric (photo) and official identification information. This data type is more sensitive than functionally required for many authentication purposes.
assumptions: Full government ID images are stored rather than extracted data fields

title: Excessive data granularity in ID images
description: Storing full government ID images captures more granular detail than may be needed (e.g., full photo, all text fields, security features) when only specific data points might be required for authentication.
assumptions: Full image storage rather than extracted data fields

title: Extended retention of government ID images
description: Government ID images may be stored longer than functionally needed for authentication purposes, creating unnecessary privacy risk over time.
assumptions: No clear retention policy specified for ID images
uncertainty_note: Retention period not specified in flow description

title: Data subject unawareness of ID image storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored in a file system, or the extent of this storage and its duration.
assumptions: Privacy notice may not clearly communicate image storage

title: Lack of control over ID image erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification or erasure of their government ID images once stored in the file system.
assumptions: No clear mechanism for data subject access/erasure requests

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing full government ID images may violate GDPR data minimization principle if only specific data fields are needed for authentication rather than complete images.
assumptions: Full images stored when extracted data might suffice

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Government ID images may be stored longer than necessary for the authentication purpose, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: No clear retention policy for ID images
uncertainty_note: Retention period not specified

title: JWT enables linking across sessions
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains user identifiers that can be used to link user activities across different sessions and potentially across different parts of the application or system.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying claims

title: JWT contains user identifier
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification of the user.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims

title: Sensitive authentication data stored in accessible location
description: JWTs contain authentication credentials which are sensitive data. Storing them in localStorage makes them accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, which may be more sensitive than functionally required.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to page JavaScript

title: JWT may persist longer than needed
description: JWTs stored in localStorage persist until explicitly cleared, which may be longer than the functional need for authentication state, violating storage limitation.
assumptions: JWTs are not automatically cleared when session ends

title: Users unaware of JWT storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage, which persists across browser sessions.
assumptions: No explicit user notification about localStorage usage

title: Limited user control over JWT removal
description: Users may lack easy control to rectify or erase JWTs stored in localStorage, requiring manual browser intervention or specific application functionality.
assumptions: No built-in logout/clear mechanism exposed to users

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage without automatic expiration may violate GDPR storage limitation principle if tokens persist longer than necessary for authentication purposes.
assumptions: JWTs lack automatic expiration or cleanup
uncertainty_note: Depends on JWT expiration configuration and cleanup mechanisms

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management
description: Storing authentication tokens in localStorage is a known security vulnerability that could lead to privacy breaches through XSS attacks, indicating insufficient cybersecurity risk management.
assumptions: No additional security measures like HttpOnly flags or secure storage alternatives

title: Sensitive child history data disclosed
description: Child history data is inherently sensitive personal data. The process P3 shares this data with the parent, which may include sensitive information about the child's activities, behaviors, or development that could be perceived as highly sensitive.
assumptions: Child history data contains sensitive personal information about the child

title: Excessive volume of child history data
description: The process may retrieve and share an excessive amount of child history data beyond what is functionally needed for parent review, potentially including historical data that is no longer relevant.
assumptions: The system retrieves full child history rather than filtered or summarized data

title: Linking through quasi-identifiers in child history
description: Child history data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., age, school, activities, dates) that could be combined to uniquely identify the child or link this data to other datasets about the child.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that could serve as quasi-identifiers

title: Revealing attributes in child history data
description: The child history data contains revealing attributes that support identification of the child data subject, such as specific activities, locations, or behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Child history includes specific identifying details about the child

title: Child unaware of data sharing with parent
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their history data is being shared with the parent for review, particularly if the child is young or if consent mechanisms are not age-appropriate.
assumptions: Child may not have meaningful awareness or consent mechanisms in place

title: Child lacks control over data sharing preferences
description: The child data subject may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their history data is processed and shared with the parent.
assumptions: System does not provide child-appropriate consent or preference mechanisms

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing full child history data may violate GDPR data minimization principles if more data is processed than is actually needed for the parent review functionality.
assumptions: System shares more data than functionally necessary for parent review
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation of data retrieval

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Processing of child personal data may not rely on valid consent, particularly if the child is below the age of digital consent or if parental consent mechanisms are not properly implemented.
assumptions: Child data processing requires valid consent under applicable regulations
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and age of child
